title: Integrations
description: The apps your account works with, and the apps your agents can work in during a call.
info: Your account's apps send alerts and sync data. App directory servers give agents tools: during a call an agent can look things up and make changes in them, using only the tools you switch on.

native.heading: Your account's apps
native.info: Alerts, exports and syncs for your account. These work on their own; agents do not call them during a call.

meetings.heading: Meetings
meetings.info: Agents join Zoom, Google Meet and Teams meetings through your own Attendee account, which bills you for bot hours.
meetings.name: Meetings
meetings.tagline: Join Zoom, Google Meet and Teams meetings

directory.heading: App directory
directory.info: Apps with an official MCP server, ready to connect. For anything else, add a custom MCP server.
directory.customHint: Paste the remote MCP URL of any app or your own backend. Headers and OAuth sign-in both work.
directory.customLine: Any app or backend, by its MCP URL
directory.noMatch: No app matches. Add it as a custom MCP server if it has one.

connect.notInDirectoryTitle: That app is not in the directory
connect.oauthLine: You will sign in to {app} and approve access. {appName} registers itself with {app} automatically, so there is nothing to set up first.
connect.noKeyNeeded: No account or key is needed.
connect.keysEncrypted: Keys are encrypted and never shown again.
connect.ownClientLine: {app} does not let apps register themselves, so connect it through an app of your own. It takes a few minutes, once.
connect.whatAgentsCanDo: What agents can do with it
connect.recommendedInfo: The tools a phone agent needs most are switched on when you connect. You can change them afterwards.
connect.readOnlyInfo: Tools the app marks read-only are switched on when you connect. Choose the rest afterwards.
connect.confirmInfo: Before using a tool that changes data, the agent asks the caller to confirm.
connect.examplesNote: Examples from {app}’s documentation. Not the live list.
connect.examplesNoteCount: Examples from {app}’s documentation, of about {count}. Not the live list.
connect.oauthToolsLine: {app} lists its tools only after you sign in. The full list is read from {app} the moment the sign-in comes back, and you choose from it on the next screen.
connect.fillFormLine: Fill in the form and the tool list is read from {app} before you connect.
connect.liveUnavailable: The live tool list is not available. These are examples from the app's documentation.

server.authNoneHint: A public server, or one whose URL carries its key.
server.authHeadersHint: A token the server expects on every request.
server.authOauthHint: You sign in to the app and approve access.
server.oauthConnected: Connected. The server’s tools have been read.
server.savedConnectNext: Saved. Now connect it: sign in so {appName} can use this server.
server.toolAccessSaved: Tool access saved. Calls that start from now on use it.
server.deleteDescription: Agents can no longer use its tools. This cannot be undone.
server.deleteDescriptionUsed: {count, plural, one {# agent uses it and will lose its tools.} other {# agents use it and will lose its tools.}} This cannot be undone.
server.description: Which of its tools agents may use during a call.
server.newDescription: Paste the app’s remote MCP endpoint.
server.newInfo: Its tools are read as soon as you save. Popular apps are set up for you on the Integrations page.
server.needsAuthLine: This server asks you to sign in before {appName} can use it.
server.notReachedLine: The server has not been reached yet.
server.readyOnly: Agents only use servers that are Ready.
server.name: Name
server.nameHint: The agent is told this name, so use the one a caller would say.
server.urlHint: The app's remote MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP or SSE).
server.savedKeepBlank: Saved. Leave blank to keep it.
server.encrypted: Values are encrypted and never shown again.
server.oauthHelp: Save, then press Connect and sign in to the app. Most servers register {appName} automatically; for one that does not, add your own app's client id below.
server.transportHint: Auto tries Streamable HTTP, then SSE. Change it only if the server needs one.
server.toolsInfo: Only switched-on tools are offered to agents. Before using a tool that changes data, the agent asks the caller to confirm.
server.noTools: No tools yet. Connect the server, then refresh.
server.noReadOnly: This server does not mark any tool as read-only, so none were switched on for you. Choose the ones agents may use.
server.agentsUsingNone: None yet. Open an agent and pick this server under Connected apps.

hubspot.blurb: Find the caller in your CRM, log the call, and create or update contacts, deals and tasks.
hubspot.note: Accounts with Sensitive Data turned on cannot write calls, notes, tasks or meetings over MCP.

steps.1: In HubSpot, open Development, then MCP Auth Apps, and create an app.
steps.2: Add the redirect URL below to the app.
steps.3: Copy the app’s client id and client secret into the fields below.

tools.search_crm_objects: Search contacts, companies and deals, for example by phone number.
tools.manage_crm_objects: Create or update contacts, deals, calls, notes, tasks and meetings.
tools.search_owners: Find the owner a record belongs to.
tools.search_properties: List the fields a record type has.
tools.get_user_details: Who is connected, and which account.

salesforce.tagline: CRM for sales and service teams
salesforce.blurb: Look up and update any Salesforce record during a call, with SOQL and SOSL search.

steps.1: In Salesforce Setup, create an External Client App with OAuth turned on.
steps.2: Give it the scopes mcp_api and refresh_token, and add the redirect URL below as its callback URL.
steps.3: Copy its consumer key (client id) and consumer secret into the fields below.

tools.find: Search across records, for example by phone number.
tools.createSobjectRecord: Create a record, such as a lead, task or case.

gohighlevel.blurb: Find and update contacts, read calendar events, move opportunities and send messages in a sub-account.
gohighlevel.note: This server has no tool to book an appointment yet.
gohighlevel.help: Create a Private Integration Token in the sub-account with the contacts, calendars, opportunities and conversations scopes.

token.label: Private Integration Token
token.hint: Settings, then Private Integrations, in the sub-account.

locationId.label: Location id
locationId.hint: The sub-account id, from Settings, then Business Profile.

tools.conversations_send-a-new-message: Send an SMS or email to a contact.

pipedrive.blurb: Find people by phone, add leads and deals, and log calls and notes.

tools.searchPersons: Find a person, for example by phone number.
tools.addActivity: Log a call or schedule a meeting.

close.blurb: Search leads, read contacts, and create leads, notes, tasks and opportunities.
close.note: Signed in with read and safe-write access. Updating existing records needs Close’s destructive scope, which is not asked for.

attio.blurb: Read and update records, lists, notes and tasks in Attio.

tools.Records: Search, read, create and update people, companies and deals.

monday.blurb: Find items on a board, create items and update their columns.
monday.note: The account needs the “monday MCP” app installed from the monday marketplace.

tools.get_board_schema: Read a board’s columns and groups.
tools.create_update: Post an update on an item.

apollo.blurb: Look up and enrich contacts, log calls and create tasks and deals in Apollo.

tools.apollo_people_match: Enrich a person. Spends Apollo credits.

zoho.blurb: Read and write Zoho CRM records through a server you set up in Zoho MCP.
zoho.note: Tool calls use your Zoho API credits.

url.label: Zoho MCP server URL
url.hint: Create a server at mcp.zoho.com with the Zoho CRM tools, then copy its URL. The URL contains its key, so keep it private.

tools.Data Operations: Create, read, update and search records in any module.
tools.Data Insights: Read-only questions about your CRM data.

calcom.blurb: Check free slots and book, reschedule or cancel meetings while the caller is on the line.

tools.get_event_types: List the meeting types you offer.

calendly.blurb: Read open times, book an invitee into a slot, or send a single-use booking link.
calendly.note: There is no reschedule tool; the agent cancels and books again.

tools.meetings-create_invitee: Book a slot. Paid Calendly plans only.

google-calendar.blurb: Read free time, suggest a slot and create or change events in Google Calendar.

steps.1: Join the Google Workspace Developer Preview Program. The Calendar MCP server is in preview.
steps.2: In a Google Cloud project, enable the Google Calendar API and the Calendar MCP API.
steps.3: Create an OAuth client of type Web application and add the redirect URL below.
steps.4: Copy its client id and client secret into the fields below.

intercom.blurb: Find the customer, read their conversations and help articles, and leave an internal note.
intercom.note: Australian workspaces are not supported by Intercom’s server.

tools.add_internal_note: Leave a note for your team.

freshdesk.blurb: Find the contact, read their tickets, and open, update or reply to a ticket.
freshdesk.note: Freshdesk caps MCP actions per plan.
freshdesk.help: Use the API key of an agent who can see the tickets the phone agent should work with.

key.label: API key
key.hint: Profile settings, then View API key.

helpscout.blurb: Read the customer’s conversations and your Docs articles. Read-only.
helpscout.note: Needs a Standard, Plus or Pro plan. The server cannot create tickets or notes.

gorgias.blurb: Read tickets and customers, reply, and add internal notes in Gorgias.

tools.Tickets: Read tickets, reply, set status and priority.

stripe.blurb: Look up customers, invoices and subscriptions, and create a payment link to text the caller.
stripe.note: Live or test mode is chosen on Stripe’s sign-in screen. Refunds wait for someone to approve them in Stripe.

tools.stripe_api_search: Find the API call for a task.
tools.stripe_api_read: Read customers, charges, invoices and subscriptions.
tools.stripe_api_write: Create a payment link, invoice or refund.

paypal.blurb: Create and send invoices, look up transactions and orders, and check disputes.

razorpay.blurb: Create and send payment links, including UPI, and look up payments, orders and refunds.
razorpay.note: Refunds cannot be made over Razorpay’s hosted server.
razorpay.help: Generate an API key in the Razorpay Dashboard under Account & Settings, then API keys. Test keys work too.

tools.send_payment_link: Send a link by SMS or email.

dodopayments.blurb: Create checkouts and payment links, and look up customers and payments in Dodo Payments.
dodopayments.note: Dodo’s sign-in screen asks for your API key and test or live mode. The execute tool can do anything your key can, including refunds, so switch it on only if you mean to.

tools.search_docs: Find the Dodo SDK call for a task.
tools.execute: Run code against the Dodo SDK: checkouts, payment links, customers, refunds.

klaviyo.blurb: Find or update a profile, subscribe the caller, and add them to a list.
klaviyo.note: The person who connects must be an Owner, Admin or Manager in Klaviyo.

tools.add_profiles_to_list: Add a profile to a list.

slack.blurb: Post a message to a channel or person when a call needs a human, and search your workspace.

steps.1: At api.slack.com/apps, create an app in your workspace. Slack only lets internal or directory apps use MCP.
steps.2: Under OAuth & Permissions, add the redirect URL below and the user token scopes the agent needs, such as chat:write and search:read.public.
steps.3: Copy the app’s client id and client secret into the fields below. A workspace admin may need to approve it.

notion.blurb: Search your pages and databases for answers, and add pages or database rows.

linear.blurb: Open an issue from a call, or check the status of one.

clickup.blurb: Create and update tasks, and search your workspace.

airtable.blurb: Look up and add records in your bases: orders, bookings, inventory, anything you keep there.

asana.blurb: Create follow-up tasks from a call and check on existing ones.

steps.1: In the Asana developer console, create an MCP app.
steps.2: Add the redirect URL below, and set distribution to the workspaces that will use it.
steps.3: Copy its client id and client secret into the fields below.

todoist.blurb: Add a to-do from a call, or read what is due.

tools.find-tasks-by-date: What is due on a day.

zapier.blurb: Reach the apps you use through Zapier: the actions you switch on in Zapier become tools.
zapier.note: Each tool call costs 2 Zapier tasks. Choose actions in Zapier, then refresh the tools here.

tools.Your Zapier actions: Each action you enable in Zapier MCP, such as “Create Google Sheets row”.

make.blurb: Run your Make scenarios as tools: each active, on-demand scenario is one tool.
make.note: A scenario must answer within 25 seconds to be useful on a call; Make keeps longer ones running in the background.

tools.Your scenarios: Each active scenario set to run on demand.

n8n.blurb: Run your n8n workflows and read its data tables, on n8n Cloud or your own instance.
n8n.help: Turn on Instance-level MCP in n8n settings, create an access token there, and expose the workflows the agent may run.

instance.label: n8n address
instance.hint: Settings, then Instance-level MCP, shows the full URL.

tools.insert_data_table_records: Add rows to a data table.

home-assistant.blurb: Check sensors and the thermostat, and switch lights and devices, in a home or property run on Home Assistant.
home-assistant.note: Caller id can be faked and a caller can try to talk the agent into things. Do not expose locks, alarms or garage doors to voice assistants, and only switch on the tools that change devices for an agent that checks who it is talking to. Only the read tool is on to start with.
home-assistant.help: Add the Model Context Protocol Server integration in Home Assistant first. The agent only sees the devices you expose to voice assistants (Settings, then Voice assistants, then Expose).

instance.label: Home Assistant address
instance.hint: Its public https address. Home Assistant Cloud gives every instance one; a local address such as homeassistant.local cannot be reached.

token.label: Long-lived access token
token.hint: Your Home Assistant profile, then Security, then Long-lived access tokens.

tools.GetLiveContext: Read the current state of exposed devices and sensors.
tools.HassTurnOn: Turn a device or area on.
tools.HassTurnOff: Turn a device or area off.
tools.HassLightSet: Set a light’s brightness or colour.

exa.blurb: Search the web and read a page when a caller asks something your prompt does not cover.
exa.note: Uses Exa’s free tier, which is rate-limited. No account needed.
